title: Find Minimum Time to Finish All Jobs II
statement:
You have `n` jobs and `n` workers, given as two arrays of the same length. `jobs[i]` is the total amount of time job `i` needs, and `workers[j]` is how much time worker `j` can put in per day.

Pair every job with exactly one worker so that each worker gets exactly one job. Workers work in parallel; worker `j` on job `i` finishes after `ceil(jobs[i] / workers[j])` days. Return the smallest number of days after which all jobs can be finished, over all possible pairings.
notes:
## Intuition

Trying all n! pairings is hopeless beyond tiny inputs. The answer is decided by the slowest pair, so we want the big jobs on the fast workers. Sorting both arrays and pairing them in order does exactly that, and an exchange argument shows it is optimal: take jobs `a <= b` and workers `x <= y`. The crossed pairing (`a` with `y`, `b` with `x`) needs `ceil(b / x)` days for one pair, which is at least both `ceil(a / x)` and `ceil(b / y)`. So uncrossing the pairs never makes the slowest pair slower, and repeating this turns any pairing into the sorted one.

## Approach

1. Sort `jobs` and `workers` in increasing order.
2. Pair `jobs[i]` with `workers[i]` for every `i`.
3. That pair needs `needed = ceil(jobs[i] / workers[i])` days.
4. Keep the largest `needed` in `days` and return it.

## Example 1, step by step

`jobs = [5, 2, 4]`, `workers = [1, 7, 5]`. Sorted: `jobs = [2, 4, 5]`, `workers = [1, 5, 7]`.

- `i = 0`: `ceil(2 / 1) = 2`, so `days = 2`.
- `i = 1`: `ceil(4 / 5) = 1`, `days` stays 2.
- `i = 2`: `ceil(5 / 7) = 1`, `days` stays 2.

The answer is `2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n) for the two sorts; the scan is O(n).
- Space: O(1) extra beyond the sorts (they work in place).

## Pitfalls

- Use the ceiling: a job of 5 with 7 per day still takes 1 full day, and 9 with 2 per day takes 5, not 4.
- In Java and C, integer `(job + worker - 1) / worker` avoids floating-point rounding.
- Pairing the biggest job with the slowest worker (sorting in opposite orders) is the worst choice, not the best.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `i` | position in both sorted arrays; job `i` goes to worker `i` |
| `needed` | days the pair at position `i` takes |
| `days` | largest `needed` so far: when every job is done |

narration.2: Sort the jobs from smallest to largest.
narration.3: Sort the workers the same way, so the biggest job meets the fastest worker.
narration.4: days tracks the slowest pair seen so far.
narration.6: Pair job i with worker i in the sorted order.
narration.7: Working workers[i] per day, this worker needs the ceiling of the job time over that rate.
narration.8: Is this pair slower than every pair so far?
narration.9: Then all jobs finish no earlier than this, so record it.
narration.12: Every job is done once the slowest pair finishes.
